unresolved.finding: The nonzero source planes RF(12,:,:) and RF(17,:,:) are omitted from both same-shard generated tables (RFveg selects planes 1-11 and RF selects 13-16 and 18), with no in-shard marker explaining whether those two populated planes are intentionally unused.
The lookup table is declared with the nonstandard `real*8` form rather than an explicit project or `iso_fortran_env` kind, making its precision compiler-dependent.
The lookup table is declared with the nonstandard `real*8` form rather than an explicit project or `iso_fortran_env` kind, making its precision compiler-dependent.

For source rank `i-1` the root uses decomposition entry `i-1`, and rank `ra` sends dimensions from entry `ra`; this conflicts with the shard's distribution template mapping rank `r` to entry `r+1`, so gathered blocks can use the preceding rank's extents, offsets, and boundary flags.
MPI return codes are overwritten without inspection, allowing communicator, datatype, collective, or free errors to cascade through invalid handles and incomplete data.
Subtracting `2*nbord` can produce zero or negative subsizes, and adjusted starts and extents are never checked against `shape(a)` or `shape(b)` before datatype creation.
A bad root for the supplied communicator aborts `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rather than `comm`, terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator invocation.
All MPI error codes are overwritten without inspection, so communicator, datatype-construction, commit, collective, or free failures can cascade into use or freeing of invalid datatype handles.

The generated MPI subarray types assume every `lm`/`ln` is positive and fits the corresponding `a` or `b` extent and every `is`/`js` start is in range, with no validation before `MPI_Type_create_subarray`.
A bad root for the supplied communicator aborts `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rather than `comm`, unexpectedly terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator that invoked this routine.

The output pointer is `intent(inout)` and is never initialized to `C_NULL_PTR`, so an unknown name or any mismatch between `chartoindex` and the generated cases returns the caller's previous or uninitialized pointer value.
For every array the template unconditionally takes `c_loc` of its lower-bound element, which does not exist when any generated variable has zero total size.
The output extent is declared with `MAXDIMS` but initialized with a fixed six-element constructor, so the template silently assumes `MAXDIMS == 6` and becomes nonconforming if that parameter changes.

There is no default case or status result for an unknown name, which therefore returns the same all-zero shape representation used for a scalar and gives the C caller no way to distinguish lookup failure.

The public C binding passes `xptr` directly to `c_f_pointer` and then dereferences the resulting Fortran pointer without checking for `C_NULL_PTR`, so a null caller pointer causes invalid pointer use instead of a controlled failure.
Names rejected by `chartoindex` return silently before the `select case`, making the advertised `Setting unknown variable` default diagnostic unreachable for the ordinary unknown-name path.

The subroutine's `iso_c_binding, only:` list omits `c_ptr` and `c_int` even though both are used, leaving successful compilation dependent on those names being host-associated by the generated enclosing unit.

Every generated logger writes arbitrary caller content and format text into a fixed-length `display` buffer without `IOSTAT`, so an overlong record or invalid format can turn logging itself into a fatal runtime I/O error.

Generated floating-point overloads use the nonstandard declaration `real*8`, whose size and generic-interface compatibility are compiler-dependent rather than tied to the project's declared real kind.
